newStructuralFinding: NOBODY WAS ASKED TO LOOK AT TARGET COUNT, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST STRUCTURAL HOLE IN THE SYSTEM. I ran the census over all 365 talent texts. Talents that DAMAGE more than one enemy with one play: deity/Destruction 3 (Set Charge d0/L1, Concussive Yield d1/L2, Fault Line d2/L3); leyline/Red 2 (Flame Surge d1/L2, Chain Detonation d5/L6); deity/Chaos 2 (Cascade Collapse d2/L3, Unravel Everything d3/L4 — but BOTH detonate "all your Omens" against a cap of "your Tier", which is 1 for the whole of levels 1-5, so both are single-target until level 6); deity/Death 1 (Necrotic Cascade d2/L3, and it triggers only on a death); deity/Civilization 1 (Magnum Opus d3/L4, 3 Actions, once per scene); deity/Order 1 (Final Decree d3/L4, 3 Actions, once per scene); deity/Power 1 (Unstoppable Advance d1/L2, and only enemies whose space you move through); leyline/Black 1 (Spoils of Isolation d2/L3, flat damage equal to your tier). **The entire heroic atlas — 150 talents, six paths, the atlas the designer's other PCs are in — has ONE: heroic/Warrior's Meteoric Leap, depth 3, Athletics 3+, level 6, 2 Actions + 2 focus, unarmed.** (Shard Training's "Shardblade Strikes graze additional targets" is a second, but it is gated on "Access to a Shardblade and Shardplate", a GM-granted reward outside the fence.) Agent, Envoy, Hunter, Leader and Scholar have literally zero. leyline/White, leyline/Blue, leyline/Green, deity/Life, deity/Fate, deity/Knowledge and deity/Sovereignty have zero. That is fourteen of twenty-one trees that can never hit two enemies at once, at any level, with any talent. Within levels 1-5 the survivors shrink further: exactly two trees have a repeatable, unconditional multi-enemy damage play before level 6 — deity/Destruction (Set Charge, level 1) and leyline/Red (Flame Surge, level 2). Everything else is conditional on a death, on movement, on a Tier-2 token cap, or is a once-per-scene level-4 capstone. AND THE ONE LEYLINE TREE THAT LOOKS LIKE AN EXCEPTION IS BUILT BACKWARDS. leyline/Black's only multi-target talent, Spoils of Isolation, reads "Each Weakened character within Attunement Range takes vital damage equal to your tier." I grepped all 365 for Weakened application: it is produced by exactly four talents, and Black's two — the Black Leyline Attunement Key ("enemies you can see within Attunement Range **with no ally within 5 feet** become Weakened") and Sapping Hex ("When you hit an **Isolated** character (one with no ally within 5 feet), it becomes Weakened") — both require the target to be standing apart from every other enemy. So Black's area attack scales with how SPREAD OUT the enemies are and does nothing against a clump: an inverted AoE, the exact opposite of the situation area damage exists to solve. The other two Weakened sources are deity/Order's Sealed Edict (level 6) and deity/Power's Absolute Authority (only on a failed test), neither of which a Black character holds. This matters more than any damage-distribution figure in the review, because it is not a balance question — it is an encounter-design constraint. It says the GM cannot put four enemies on the table without the fight becoming a queue, and it says so for the specific party this review was commissioned about. It also interacts with the "up to your tier" cap that the good-at-something critic found in seven deity trees: the deity atlas's answer to groups is gated behind the same level-6 wall as everything else. Nothing settles what the right target-count budget is without adversary statblocks (are groups of minions the norm?), which is out of scope — but the census itself is entirely inside the fence and nobody ran it.

contradictions.resolution: The advantage-economy critic is right that there is no single behaviour, and there is a THIRD data point neither of the other two found: the temp-HP handler in `data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json` carries its own description — "The payload: the Exalted ally also gains Temp HP = [Tier][Die on White] — **keeps the higher ('does not stack')**, GM-relayed." So a per-talent authored rule asserts keep-the-higher on the very talent whose swing deity-parity deleted using overwrite-even-if-smaller. Three behaviours are in circulation across two engine files and one authored description. Note the scope caveat none of the three flagged: this is an engine question, not a 365-talent question, and it should be filed as a ruling (unify the writers, then decide) rather than being used as arithmetic in any tree comparison until it is unified.

contradictions.between: damage-distribution ("Momentum's Edge has THREE readings, not two"), intent-drift ("'Speed' means movement-in-feet in six other talents; it is a live balance bug worth +20-30"), and the good-at-something critic (which refuted "delivers nothing")

contradictions.resolution: Nobody has settled it and nobody can settle it from talent text alone, which is the honest answer that should be reported. damage-distribution's three-world framing is the correct epistemic position: `@movement.walk.rate` is a DerivedValueField, "Speed" is used as a movement rate in feet in Forge Construct and Walking Ruin AND as a tested skill in Concussive Yield and Inevitable Snare, so the readings are (a) resolves to nothing, (b) ~+25-30 flat impact, (c) ~+2 to +5 skill modifier. intent-drift's confident "it is a balance bug worth +20-30" overstates. The advantage-economy critic verified five distinct misclassifications in the advantage row alone (Bonds of Community and Anticipate missed; Bulwark Ground double-counted; Natural Order typed as consumer when it denies; three Gain-Advantage action-riders typed as consumers), the disadvantage row misses Warrior's Defensive Position, and the plot-die row is wrong by six. The Destruction ranking, on friendly fire. deity/Destruction is ranked #2 or #3 in the deity atlas on 'the highest floor, no-roll no-save damage', and the deity-parity critic correctly noted that Set Charge, Concussive Yield and Fault Line all read 'each character', not 'each enemy'. Nobody has priced that. Set Charge's radius is 10 ft and the placer chooses the point; Fault Line is a 60 ft line originating from the caster. In a melee party this is not a rounding error, and it is the single largest unpriced discount in the deity rankings.

Any deity ranking that treats Chaos's Cascade Collapse and Unravel Everything as area effects at levels 1-5. Both detonate 'all your Omens', and Reaper's-Harvest-style tier caps apply — the Omen cap equals your Tier, which is 1 through level 5. Both talents are single-target for the entire level range this review is about. The good-at-something critic found the tier-cap flattening in seven deity trees; nobody applied it back to the damage rankings.

The whole heroic-vs-leyline power comparison, until it is re-run. Not because the conclusions are wrong, but because every one of them was computed against a level column that has since been corrected and no analysis has re-derived a single figure from the new file.
